title: Synthesis, structure and characterisation of Ln5O(OPri)13 with Ln = Nd, Gd or Er

synthesis.procedure: Under dry oxygen-free argon in a glove-box, 12.79 mmol (0.500 g) K was dissolved in 20 mL of 1:1 (v/v) toluene–2-propanol, followed by 0.85 mL of 1 M water in the same solvent. After 1 h, 4.263 mmol NdCl3 was added. After 48 h at room temperature the mixture was centrifuged to remove KCl. Evaporation of the solution gave a mass consisting almost exclusively of Nd5O(OPri)13. Dissolution in hexane, centrifugation of a very small amount of solid, and evaporation of the solvent yielded highly pure crystalline 1. SEM-EDS showed no K or Cl contamination. The NdCl3 source was important: reaction proceeded at room temperature with the Strem 99.9% anhydrous chloride, but another source gave no reaction even after two weeks at 75 °C.

properties.summary: UV-Vis spectra of 1 in toluene–2-propanol (190–900 nm) show typical Nd3+ f–f absorptions; hypersensitive 4G5/2,2G7/2 ← 4I9/2 (550–630 nm) and 4D1/2,4D3/2,4D5/2 ← 4I9/2 (340–380 nm) fine structure is used for identification and is unchanged from pure toluene to toluene–2-propanol (1:9), indicating no formation of a solvated Nd5O(OPri)13(HOPri)2 species. Reaction of 1 with Al4(OPri)12 (Nd:Al = 1:3) is slow at room temperature but complete after 2 h at 80 °C to NdAl3(OPri)12 as monitored by UV-Vis.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to 1: under dry oxygen-free argon, 12.79 mmol (0.500 g) K was dissolved in 20 mL of 1:1 (v/v) toluene–2-propanol, followed by 0.85 mL of 1 M water in the same solvent. After 1 h, 4.263 mmol GdCl3 was added. After 48 h at room temperature, KCl was removed by centrifugation. Evaporation, hexane dissolution, centrifugation, and evaporation gave highly pure crystalline 2 in 90–95% yield. SEM-EDS showed no K or Cl contamination.

properties.summary: Gd3+ (f7) absorptions are weak and only in the UV, where they are obscured by 2-propanol; no usable UV-Vis identification spectrum of 2 is reported. After 2 h at 80 °C, a Gd:Al = 1:3 mixture of 2 and Al4(OPri)12 evaporates to GdAl3(OPri)12 (IR/SEM-EDS), but this is a subsequent conversion rather than an optical measurement of 2 itself.

synthesis.procedure: Obtained as a co-product of an erbium–aluminium 2-propoxide. Under dry oxygen-free argon, 25.58 mmol (1.000 g) K was dissolved in 20 mL of 1:1 (v/v) toluene–2-propanol, followed by 1.70 mL of 1 M water in the same solvent. Then 1.71 mmol Al(OPri)3 (0.348 g) and 8.526 mmol (2.333 g) ErCl3 were added. After 48 h at room temperature the mixture was centrifuged to remove KCl. Slow evaporation of the pink solution gave a crystal mixture of an Er–Al alkoxide with Er:Al ≈ 3:1 and Er5O(OPri)13. SEM-EDS showed no K or Cl contamination. Abstract stoichiometry is equivalently described as 15 KOPri + H2O + Al(OPri)3 with 5 ErCl3 in toluene–2-propanol.

properties.summary: No new solid-state IR differences versus the previously reported orthorhombic Er5O(OPri)13; the paper states that previously reported solution UV-Vis and FT-IR of dissolved Er5O(OPri)13 should apply because the molecular units are essentially identical. Prior work cited here found reaction of Er5O(OPri)13 with Al4(OPri)12 complete after 2 h at 75 °C.
